Structure largely aligns with the guidance excerpt, but I flagged three priority issues needing confirmation before the sign‑off meeting.  
1) Liver enzyme elevations: Warnings/Precautions should explicitly state the reversible transaminase elevations seen in Phase 3 and specify monitoring/management; please confirm if we may add the standard template monitoring language—Option A (proposed for review): "Transaminase elevations: In clinical trials, reversible increases in ALT and/or AST were observed; monitor liver enzymes before and periodically during treatment and discontinue therapy if ALT or AST rise to ≥3×ULN or if clinical symptoms of liver injury occur."  
2) Hypersensitivity: The label should state immediate discontinuation and emergency care for serious allergic reactions—please confirm adding the standard hypersensitivity sentence—Option B (proposed): "Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have occurred; discontinue immediately and initiate emergency treatment if suspected."  
3) Renal impairment/Limitations of Use: The clinical summary notes no demonstrated efficacy in severe renal impairment but the Limitations section does not; please confirm adding Option C: "Efficacy has not been established in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min); use is not recommended."  

If you confirm which of these standard additions are acceptable, I will draft exact, template‑aligned insertions and plain‑language patient leaflet wording for review.
